subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory search get a default-on periodic sync fallback for silent watcher failures, or should interval sync remain opt-in with a different watcher-health mechanism?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the likely fix changes default fallback behavior and can add background indexing/provider work for existing users.

options.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
options.body: Land the linked fix shape after refreshing the branch and ensuring interval dirty marking is scoped to memory-source managers.

options.title: Keep interval sync opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at 0 and document or doctor-recommend `intervalMinutes` for users who need watcher-outage protection.

options.title: Choose watcher health instead
options.body: Reject default periodic sync and implement an explicit watcher liveness/error recovery path that does not change background sync defaults.

recommendation.title: Approve default-on fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Land the linked fix shape after refreshing the branch and ensuring interval dirty marking is scoped to memory-source managers.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent memory manager and index-state history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the fallback/default decision.
